items.title: Florida Vintage: Miami-Dade becomes first Florida region to enter 10-digit phone number era

headlines: MIAMI-DADE BECAME FIRST FLORIDA REGION WITH 10-DIGIT DIALING IN 1998
MIAMI-DADE LED FLORIDA INTO 10-DIGIT CALLING
FLORIDA STARTED TEN-DIGIT PHONE NUMBERS RIGHT HERE IN MIAMI-DADE
draft.article:
Miami-Dade holds a unique place in state history as the very first region in Florida to transition into the 10-digit phone number era.

This telecommunications milestone officially took place in the summer of 1998. Before any other region across Florida adopted the format, Miami-Dade became the earliest area in the state to leave seven-digit local dialing behind.

The summer of 1998 permanently changed how local residents placed calls, establishing Miami-Dade as the first community in all of Florida to embrace ten digits.

items.desc: The CBS News Miami NEXT Weather team is urging residents not to drive, walk or wade through the saltwater flooding.

headlines: KING TIDES AND HIGH WINDS BRING COASTAL FLOODING TO MIAMI
MAJOR COASTAL FLOOD WARNING ISSUED FOR SOUTH FLORIDA
WHY MIAMI STREETS ARE FLOODING UNDER TUESDAY MORNING TIDES
draft.article:
Miami faces significant coastal flooding Tuesday as king tides peak at 10:07 a.m. Fort Lauderdale will see its high tide at 10:21 a.m. A coastal flood warning remains active across South Florida, alongside a wind advisory featuring northeast winds of 15 to 25 mph and gusts up to 45 mph along the coast.

Scattered downpours bring a Level 1 risk for street flooding through Wednesday. Residents are warned not to walk, wade, or drive through standing saltwater, which is corrosive to cars.

Dangerous marine conditions include 12 to 15 foot seas, a gale warning through Tuesday night, and life-threatening rip currents that make ocean swimming unsafe. Temperatures will linger in the low 80s.

headlines: VICKI LOPEZ AND ROB PIPER FACE MIAMI-DADE COMMISSION RUNOFF
DISTRICT FIVE VOTERS DECIDE COUNTY COMMISSION RUNOFF
FROM BRICKELL TO SOUTH BEACH, DISTRICT FIVE CHOOSES ITS COMMISSIONER
draft.article: District 5 voters across Miami and Miami Beach are deciding a runoff election for the Miami-Dade County Commission. Appointed incumbent Vicki Lopez faces challenger Rob Piper, a Marine Corps veteran. District 5 encompasses neighborhoods including Brickell, Downtown, Little Havana, Mid Beach, Shenandoah, and South Beach. Lopez secured 42.3 percent of the vote in the August primary, while Piper earned 29.5 percent. Lopez joined the commission following a 7-5 vote after Eileen Higgins stepped down. Lopez highlights her state legislative work on condo oversight and the Live Local Act. Piper is campaigning against current development concessions, calling for changes to the Live Local Act to protect local planning.

headlines: KING TIDE FLOODING THREATENS SOUTH FLORIDA THROUGH OCTOBER 31
SEVERE TIDES AND RAIN BRING MAJOR FLOOD THREAT
WHY MIAMI COASTAL STREETS WILL FLOOD WORSE BY TUESDAY
draft.article:
South Florida coastal streets and parks face a rising risk of submersion as a powerful cycle of king tides continues through October 31. High water logged local areas on Friday and Saturday, driven by onshore winds that push ocean water directly onto land.

The National Weather Service office in Miami warns that the peak will hit on Tuesday, bringing the threat of moderate to major flooding.

Conditions will worsen with 1 to 2 inches of rain forecast along the coastline over the coming days. Meteorologist Donal Harrigan warned that incoming showers will amplify water levels in areas already dealing with the high tides.

DISCOVER THE 1825 LIGHTHOUSE BUILT TO WARN PASSING SHIPS
draft.article: The Cape Florida Lighthouse traces its local history back to 1825 on Key Biscayne. Constructed during that year, the coastal beacon was established specifically to warn passing ships navigating the waters off Key Biscayne. Key Biscayne became home to the safety structure in 1825, serving vessels that journeyed past the area. Built with the clear mission to warn ships, the Cape Florida Lighthouse stands tied to its original 1825 construction on the island.
